messages:
maya: Heads-up — FP8 warmstart canary on atlas-13b showed a weird token-level drift on H100 when cold-started behind continuous batching. small repro in canary run 3.
zane: ugh. can you paste logs? was this with KV prefetch on?
maya: Prefetch was off. We were testing the default warmstart (warmup_tokens=32), config attached. observed output mismatch with baseline int8/gptq on first ~40 tokens. after warmup it converges.
olivia: is the drift deterministic across seeds?
maya: yeah, deterministic on that shard. not across all shards. only nodes with mixed tiling (L2->L3 change) on H100. on L40S the effect is smaller but still there.
akshay: could be the tiling handshake + ephemeral accumulator init. when FP8 kernels spin up they use a per-tensor scale calc that can be non-idempotent pre-warm.
lina: do we have a minimal repro? can we force single-request (no batching) vs continuous-batching to see if it's batching-related?
maya: repro script: ```py
# warmstart repro snippet
cfg = {
  "model": "atlas-13b",
  "precision": "fp8",
  "warmup_tokens": 32,
  "continuous_batching": true,
  "kv_prefetch": false
}
# send 1 request with 200 tokens, compare first 80 tokens vs baseline
```
maya: Logs excerpt: ```
[2026-02-12T11:03:12Z] kernel:init fp8_scale=0.0032 tile_layout=8x128
[2026-02-12T11:03:12Z] kv:alloc shard=4 warmstart=false
[2026-02-12T11:03:12Z] runtime:batcher received=1 running=7
[2026-02-12T11:03:12Z] generation:token 18 mismatch baseline-delta=4.3e-3
```
zane: interesting that warmstart=false in the kv log. why wasn't prefetching active for that shard?
maya: it's because continuous_batching scheduled the request onto a worker that hadn't run a prefetch for that model variant — race between batcher and prefetch task.
olivia: hypothesis: the FP8 kernel's dynamic rescale path runs first token differently when accumulators aren't zeroed, causing a tiny offset that gets amplified over autoregressive steps.
akshay: workaround ideas: 1) force kv_prefetch true for canaries 2) bump warmup_tokens to 128 3) disable continuous_batching for first N requests 4) zero-accumulators on kernel init
lina: can we test 2 & 3 quickly on canary?
maya: started a run with warmup_tokens=128 + continuous_batching=false on the same shard. deploy-bot: Canary deployment 4477000000-2 started (fp8, warmup=128, no-continuous-batching) :rocket:
sre-bot: Note: ammeter metrics will be collected to trace token-level drift.
akshay: also try setting fp8_dynamic_scale=true in runtime to make rescale deterministic across cold-starts.
maya: added that in a parallel canary: warmup=32 + fp8_dynamic_scale=true. queued.
zane: results?
maya: quick summary: warmup=128/no-batching -> drift gone on H100 shard. warmup=32/dynamic-scale -> reduced but not eliminated; still 1e-3 per-token delta for first ~20 tokens. L40S had minor delta only in 32/default.
olivia: sounds like a mitigation matrix: prefer warmup>=64 for H100 in mixed-tiling clusters, or disable continuous_batching for first requests until model state is primed.
lina: operational impact? longer p99 latency for first requests if we bump warmup.
akshay: tradeoff: slight startup latency vs correctness. can we instead run a synchronous priming request (shadow warmstart) on new workers before routing real traffic? cheaper than warming all requests.
maya: I prototyped a shadow-warmstart: POST /prime with head_tokens=200 on worker spin-up. reduces customer-visible latency and avoids global warmup token increase.
zane: ok file a small RFC for defaulting fp8_canary_policy: {"warmup_tokens": 64, "shadow_warmstart": true, "fp8_dynamic_scale": true} and include experiment results. keep this in canary for one week.
maya: will do. I'll post perf numbers + token-delta heatmap to the canary dashboard. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
olivia: also add a note to the onboarding runbook: "When enabling FP8 on mixed-tiling H100 clusters, run shadow-warmstart on worker init".
akshay: we should also add a unit test in kernel init that zeros accumulators and validates rescale-consistency on CPU emulation.
lina: tagging @eng-runtime for follow-up on batching heuristics.
maya: thanks — follow-ups: create RFC, update canary config, add kernel init test.
